motion_provenance.source: powerliftingtechnique.com (grip a thumb's length outside the shoulders, vertical forearms, straight wrists); barbend.com (grip slightly wider than shoulders); stronglifts.com (vertical bar path, elbows under the bar, shrug at the top); trainheroic.com and Starting Strength (bar over the mid-foot, head through after the bar passes the forehead); muscleandstrength.com ('through the window'); humankinetics.com (move the body around the bar); builtwithscience.com, livestrong.com (lower-back arch is the main fault; squeeze glutes, quads, abs); ExRx 'Barbell Military Press' (press until the arms are extended overhead, lower to the front of the neck)

start_position: Feet about hip width, glutes and abs tight
Bar on the front of the shoulders, hands just outside them, forearms vertical
concentric: Press straight up; move your head back to let the bar pass
Once the bar passes your forehead, push your head through
top_hold: Arms straight beside the ears, bar over the middle of the feet; shrug up
eccentric: Head back again, lower the bar to the collarbones under control

validation_profile.comment: Thresholds for automated checks. They catch defects in the animation data (jumps, slides, penetration, asymmetry). They do not certify exercise technique; that needs a qualified human.
validation_profile.max_hand_into_bar_comment: The skin of the palm is rigid in this rig. Up to 8 mm of palm pad inside the bar stands for soft tissue pressed flat by the load; more than that, or any finger passing through the bar, is a defect.
validation_profile.max_elbow_flexion_comment: Front rack of a strict press: the bar rests on the collarbones and the elbow closes to about 150 deg (AAOS active elbow range 0-150). The default 145 kept the bar 20 cm in front of the chest (23/11 side view vs video 5cSo71oxLVc).

technical_cues: Grip just outside the shoulders, wrists straight
Squeeze glutes and abs; do not lean back
Bar travels straight up over the middle of the feet
Head back as the bar passes, then through at the top
common_mistakes: Leaning back and arching the lower back to finish the press
Grip too wide, elbows flared straight out
Pressing the bar forward around the face instead of moving the head
muscle_roles_note: Three levels (Kiệt 15/11). Standing barbell press: shoulder flexion/abduction plus elbow extension; anterior and lateral deltoid carry it, triceps extend the elbow, upper trapezius and serratus rotate the shoulder blade upward (the shrug at lockout); standing, the trunk (abs, obliques, erectors, glutes) holds the body rigid under the bar (ExRx 'Barbell Military Press' target / synergists / stabilizers).
